classification.difficultyReason: Compare the square of the longest side with the sum of the other two squares, then identify the opposite angle.

content.prompt: For each triangle shown below, decide whether it is a right-angled triangle. If it is, name the right angle.

spec.description: B is lower left, C lower right and A above C. Preserve the visually perpendicular drawing without adding a right-angle marker. Decorative blue source strokes become house black.
spec.mathematics: AB=10, AC=8, BC=7; all three givens are retained.
spec.answerVisibility: Side lengths and vertex names are permanent givens; no answer marks appear.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}7^2+8^2&=49+64\\7^2+8^2&=113\\10^2&=100\end{align*}$$
Since $7^2+8^2\ne10^2$, the triangle is not right-angled.

spec.description: C is upper left, B upper right and A below C. No right-angle marker is supplied. Decorative blue source strokes become house black.
spec.answerVisibility: Side lengths and vertex names are permanent givens; no answer marks appear.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}3^2+4^2&=9+16\\3^2+4^2&=25\\5^2&=25\end{align*}$$
Since $3^2+4^2=5^2$, the triangle is right-angled by the converse of Pythagoras’ theorem. The angle opposite $AB$ is $\angle BCA=90^\circ$.

spec.description: C is left, B upper right and A lower right. No right-angle marker is supplied. Decorative blue source strokes become house black.
spec.answerVisibility: Side lengths and vertex names are permanent givens; no answer marks appear.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}10^2+24^2&=100+576\\10^2+24^2&=676\\26^2&=676\end{align*}$$
Since $10^2+24^2=26^2$, the triangle is right-angled by the converse of Pythagoras’ theorem. The angle opposite $BC$ is $\angle BAC=90^\circ$.
